\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಲಾರಿ} (lāri)}{ಲಾರಿ (lāri)}]{\kn{ಲಾರಿ} (lāri) — a lorry; a truck}

\label{lesson:KA-C451-lari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to break down, then the Kannada for repair work.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಲಾರಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಲಾರಿ}} — \emph{lāri} — \textquotedblleft{}a lorry; a truck\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಲಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ತರಕಾರಿ} \kn{ಹಳ್ಳಿಯಿಂದ} \kn{ನಗರಕ್ಕೆ} \kn{ಬರುತ್ತದೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lāriyalli tarakāri haḷḷiyinda nagarakke baruttade.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Vegetables come from the village to the city by lorry.
\end{quote}

Plural: \kn{ಲಾರಿಗಳು}, \emph{lārigaḷu}.

The plural takes -\kn{ಗಳು}: \kn{ಲಾರಿಗಳು}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಲಾರಿ}} (\emph{lāri}) is a loan from English \emph{lorry}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lāri}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lāri}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lāriyalli tarakāri haḷḷiyinda nagarakke baruttade.} — Vegetables come from the village to the city by lorry.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to break down, then the Kannada for repair work, then say \emph{lāri} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಲಾರಿ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A lorry; a truck\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಜೀಪು} (jīpu)}{ಜೀಪು (jīpu)}]{\kn{ಜೀಪು} (jīpu) — a jeep}

\label{lesson:KA-C451-jipu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for repair work, then the Kannada for a lorry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಜೀಪು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಜೀಪು}} — \emph{jīpu} — \textquotedblleft{}a jeep\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಕಾಡಿನ} \kn{ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಜೀಪು} \kn{ಮಾತ್ರ} \kn{ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāḍina dāriyalli jīpu mātra hōguttade.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Only a jeep can go on the forest track.
\end{quote}

Written with a final -\kn{ು}, as older loans often are.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಜೀಪು}} (\emph{jīpu}) is a loan from English \emph{jeep}, written with a final -\emph{u}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jīpu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jīpu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāḍina dāriyalli jīpu mātra hōguttade.} — Only a jeep can go on the forest track.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for repair work, then the Kannada for a lorry, then say \emph{jīpu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಟ್ಯಾಕ್ಸಿ} (ṭyāksi)}{ಟ್ಯಾಕ್ಸಿ (ṭyāksi)}]{\kn{ಟ್ಯಾಕ್ಸಿ} (ṭyāksi) — a taxi}

\label{lesson:KA-C451-tyaksi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a lorry, then the Kannada for a jeep.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಟ್ಯಾಕ್ಸಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಟ್ಯಾಕ್ಸಿ}} — \emph{ṭyāksi} — \textquotedblleft{}a taxi\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ರಾತ್ರಿ} \kn{ತಡವಾದ್ದರಿಂದ} \kn{ನಾವು} \kn{ಟ್ಯಾಕ್ಸಿ} \kn{ಹಿಡಿದೆವು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rātri taḍavāddarinda nāvu ṭyāksi hiḍidevu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because it was late at night we took a taxi.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಟ್ಯಾಕ್ಸಿ} \kn{ಹಿಡಿ}, to catch a taxi.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಟ್ಯಾಕ್ಸಿ}} (\emph{ṭyāksi}) is a loan from English \emph{taxi}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a lorry, then the Kannada for a jeep, then say \emph{ṭyāksi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಬೈಕ್} (baik)}{ಬೈಕ್ (baik)}]{\kn{ಬೈಕ್} (baik) — a motorbike}

\label{lesson:KA-C451-baik}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a jeep, then the Kannada for a taxi.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಬೈಕ್}}
\textbf{\kn{ಬೈಕ್}} — \emph{baik} — \textquotedblleft{}a motorbike\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ನನ್ನ} \kn{ತಮ್ಮ} \kn{ಬೈಕ್ನಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಕಚೇರಿಗೆ} \kn{ಹೋಗುತ್ತಾನೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nanna tamma baiknalli kacērige hōguttāne.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My younger brother goes to the office on a motorbike.
\end{quote}

A bicycle is a \kn{ಸೈಕಲ್}; a \kn{ಬೈಕ್} has an engine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಬೈಕ್}} (\emph{baik}) is a loan from English \emph{bike}, which in India names a motorbike.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baik}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baik}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nanna tamma baiknalli kacērige hōguttāne.} — My younger brother goes to the office on a motorbike.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a jeep, then the Kannada for a taxi, then say \emph{baik} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಬೈಕ್} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A motorbike\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಎತ್ತಿನಗಾಡಿ} (ettinagāḍi)}{ಎತ್ತಿನಗಾಡಿ (ettinagāḍi)}]{\kn{ಎತ್ತಿನಗಾಡಿ} (ettinagāḍi) — a bullock cart}

\label{lesson:KA-C451-ettinagadi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a taxi, then the Kannada for a motorbike.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಎತ್ತಿನಗಾಡಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಎತ್ತಿನಗಾಡಿ}} — \emph{ettinagāḍi} — \textquotedblleft{}a bullock cart\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಹಳ್ಳಿಯಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ರೈತರು} \kn{ಎತ್ತಿನಗಾಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಕಬ್ಬು} \kn{ಒಯ್ಯುತ್ತಾರೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{haḷḷiyalli raitaru ettinagāḍiyalli kabbu oyyuttāre.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the village farmers carry sugarcane in bullock carts.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಎತ್ತಿನ}, of an ox, plus \kn{ಗಾಡಿ}, a cart.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಎತ್ತಿನಗಾಡಿ}} (\emph{ettinagāḍi}) is a Kannada compound: \kn{ಎತ್ತಿನ}, \textquotedblleft{}of an ox\textquotedblright{}, from native \emph{ettu}, \textquotedblleft{}an ox\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 815), and \kn{ಗಾಡಿ}, \textquotedblleft{}a cart\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Hindustani \emph{gāṛī}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ettinagāḍi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ettinagāḍi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{haḷḷiyalli raitaru ettinagāḍiyalli kabbu oyyuttāre.} — In the village farmers carry sugarcane in bullock carts.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a taxi, then the Kannada for a motorbike, then say \emph{ettinagāḍi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಎತ್ತಿನಗಾಡಿ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A bullock cart\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
